name: Salt of the Earth
storyline:
You are Daisy Margherita, an elite military operative falsely accused of murder and sentenced to prison. Before prison, your rank was Lieutenant Colonel. Due to a rare genetic anomaly, you have superhuman physiology and… rabbit ears. You are regarded as one of the strongest fighters in the cosmos, second only to the Doomslayer himself. (As a result, confining you to prison has caused the UAC to incur extraordinary difficulty and expense, not to mention many injured guards.)

Recently, an ancient, malevolent, and extraordinarily powerful practitioner of black magic, known only as The Sorceress, infiltrated the Sanctum where the Doomslayer was entombed after his defeat of Davoth. There, The Sorceress absconded with the Doomslayer's crypt. The UAC has promised you a full pardon if you can defeat The Sorceress and recover the Slayer. But as your journey unfolds, you learn that taking the Slayer was but a step in The Sorceress's ultimate plan to invoke the physical rebirth of her dark and vengeful god—a primordial, cosmic destroyer hell bent on devouring creation. This entity is known only as the Lord of Salt. If the Sorceress succeeds in summoning the Lord of Salt, he will destroy all nondemon life in the universe. Only you can stop The Sorceress and save Creation.
summary: Salt of the Earth is a megawad for Doom II, targeting the MBF21 compatibility level. This early release contains maps 1-7, 10, 11, and 31 of a planned 32+ map set. The gameplay is primarily setpiece fights and BFG slaughter, but there are some reality, forced pacifist, platforming, exploration, and other elements to lend variety. The maps are fairly long and difficult, intended for players who enjoy a challenge rather than casual play.
